reasons: Status mislabeled: the rationale itself concedes Section 19 meets or exceeds the preferred position (professional/workmanlike standard, 90-day Deliverable conformity, term-long Hosted Services conformity, compliance with law, no malicious code, repair/replace/re-perform plus termination and refund, and a disclaimer carve-out for the express warranties). This should be recorded as a compliant finding, not a deviation requiring a redline.

The proposed edit is purely typographic — inserting '(90)' after the spelled-out word 'ninety' — and changes no substantive term. 'For ninety days' is already legally unambiguous, so there is no genuine risk of argument over the measured period and no playbook gap (period, remedy, or disclaimer carve-out) is being closed.

The failing deterministic check ('warranty period ≥ 90 days or expressed in months/years') is a false negative caused by the period being written in words rather than numerals; it is not evidence of a substantive shortfall and does not justify raising a negotiation issue.

Raising a cosmetic drafting point under the WARRANTY rule dilutes the negotiation position and risks reopening an otherwise favourable warranty package; if the numeral convention matters, it belongs in a non-substantive drafting clean-up, not a playbook deviation.
